chapter_theme: Samadhi (சமாதி), the eighth limb, is reached through the limbs from yama on: mind and breath dissolve together, bindu and nada rise, the gaze is turned back, and the yogi joins the Supreme in a cool absorption where Siva is the soul within. Yet for one who goes with the Lord no samadhi is needed.
structure_note: The chapter opens (618) and closes (631) with verses that turn on the word சமாதி: the first makes samadhi the fruit of the limbs, the last says union with the Lord makes it unnecessary. Between them are verses on mind and breath (620), the yogic body (621 to 627) and the state itself (628 to 630).

618.reading: Samadhi can be reached by going through yama and the limbs that follow; in them lie the eight siddhis; to those who abide in yama and the rest, samadhi comes of itself.
618.nuance: Each line turns on சமாதி யமாதி, a chime of samadhi with yama-adi (yama and the rest). The verse binds the highest limb to the first, the ethical one: there is no samadhi without yama.

619.reading: If bindu and nada rise high in Meru, they join in the samadhi where there is no juncture, and the rare substance of endless knowledge and a beautiful light appear.
619.nuance: மேரு is traditionally the spine or the crown of the head. சந்தி இல்லாத (without juncture) may mean a state with no meeting of opposites, or one beyond the junctures of time. Both bindu and nada are technical terms here.

620.reading: Where the abiding mind is, there the breath is; where the mind is not, the breath is not; for those who rejoice within the abiding mind, within it comes the dissolving of mind.
620.nuance: The verse states the yogic teaching that mind and breath move together, so stilling one stills the other. மன்மனம் may be 'the abiding mind' or simply a doubled மனம். மனோலயம் (the mind's dissolving) is the goal, reached inside the mind and not by force.

621.reading: They contemplate the opened well and the dense forest until they know them by seeing; in the open space of the ball, between the rich hills, they reined the horse with the bridle.
621.nuance: Every image is symbolic: the horse is commonly taken as the breath or mind and the rein as its control. கூபம் (well), விஞ்சத் தடவி (Vindhya forest, or dense wood) and செண்டு வெளி (open ground of the ball) are places in the yogic body that I can't fix.

622.reading: You who stay in the middle of the four doors at the summit of the root channel: once you have seen the upper door open onto space, Death's word will not reach you even in dreams.
622.nuance: மூல நாடி (root nadi) is usually the central channel and மேலை வாசல் (upper door) the opening at the crown. The last line can be read literally, that the yogi escapes death, or as freedom from fear of it; the variant முக்கடல் for முகட்டு changes line 1.

623.reading: Five mandalas, twelve bounds and forty-eight dwellers holding them, with the aim seen in the middle: there the moon shines and flows on the moving step.
623.nuance: The numbers (5, 12, six eights) map the yogic body in a way the verse does not explain; tradition takes the moon as the nectar flowing from the crown. ஓடும் பதம் is obscure. A short reading is all the Tamil supports.

624.reading: For those who lock the breath that stirs in the body as with a bolt, settle it in that ground where seeking ends, and turn the gaze back to rest within the eye, the mango in the garden hangs within reach.
624.nuance: The ripe mango hanging in one's own garden is the fruit of practice, near at hand. தேட்டற்ற நிலம் (ground without seeking) echoes 604's தேட்டமும் இல்லை. Which bodily ground is meant is not said.

625.reading: There is a way to know the form: the gods seized the dark mountain, churned and drank the nectar, but they will not climb the rare mountain and drink the nectar there; so the mind that is the holy mountain ended and ceased.
625.nuance: The contrast is between the gods' outer churning of the ocean with Mount Mandara and the inner mountain, taken as the crown of the head, where the yogi drinks nectar. Line 4 (திருவரை யாமனந் தீர்ந்தற்ற வாறே) is obscure and its word division uncertain.

626.reading: Making love the means and subduing desire, they went to the Trusted One, the First, the chanter of the four Vedas, the light shining within red gold, climbed the branch, worshipped and gathered there.
626.nuance: கொம்பேறி (having climbed the branch) is traditionally the ascent to the crown. அருத்தி may be desire (subdued) or a form of 'feeding'. The verse joins yogic ascent and devotional worship.

627.reading: Above the base is the three-sided form; at the juncture where the paths of time meet, at the upper crescent standing level with the forehead, the form takes many different forms.
627.nuance: முச்சதுரம் may be a triangle or a figure of three squares, traditionally the seat of kundalini above the base. மேலைப் பிறை (upper crescent) is the moon at the brow or crown. The verse is a map I can't fix.

628.reading: Free of imagining, going by the path of fire, seeking the splendour of the great light that made all forms and meeting it with the joined moon, one becomes the Supreme: that is cool samadhi.
628.nuance: கனல் வழி (path of fire) and புணர் மதி (the moon joined) are traditionally the rising power meeting the moon at the crown. Samadhi is called தண் (cool) after the fire of the ascent. தற்பரம் is the Supreme, or the state of being it.

629.reading: For those able to rest in absorption, when they reach the summit the tattvas gather, the fair good lady is caught as in a net, anger is broken and goes, and they stay in balance.
629.nuance: மாதுநல்லாள் may be Shakti, held within the yogi, or worldly woman, no longer a snare; the verse does not say. துலை (balance, scales) gives the image of equanimity.

630.reading: The God who stood as the single flame of light becomes both the First and the soul that stands within; the first Brahma and the one coloured like the great sea bow at the First's feet and gain love.
630.nuance: The verse identifies the light seen in samadhi with the soul within (சீவன்), a strong claim on its face. The variant முன்நின்ற (standing before) for உள்நின்ற (standing within) would weaken it. Brahma and Vishnu are shown as Siva's worshippers.

631.reading: Many yogas suit those who practise samadhi; if one goes with the Lord, no samadhis are needed; if one becomes him, there is no samadhi at all; yet in samadhi all sixty-four siddhis are attained.
631.nuance: The verse ranks three states: practising samadhi, going with the Lord, and becoming him, where samadhi has no meaning. எட்டெட்டு (eight eights) is read as sixty-four; it could also mean the eight siddhis in each of their kinds. The last line restores samadhi's worth after relativizing it.

links.note: 552 lists the eight limbs from yama to samadhi; 618 draws the consequence that samadhi is reached only through yama and the rest, so the ethical limbs are the way to the highest.
618 makes samadhi the fruit of the limbs; 631 says that for one who goes with the Lord samadhi is not needed and for one who becomes him there is none, so the chapter's goal is itself relative.
583 calls closing the lower door and fixing the mind on the upper one the way to conquer time; 622 says that once the upper door opens Death's word is not heard even in dreams.
The Kural says those who have won the power of austerity can even leap past Death; Tirumular names a yogic means, the upper door seen open, for the same escape.

The Naladiyar says no one here has leapt clear of Death and escaped, so give your wealth now; Tirumular says the yogi who sees the upper door will not hear Death even in dreams. The conflict holds on the literal reading of 622, that the yogi escapes death; if it means only freedom from fear of death, it dissolves.

604 sets the two gazes at the middle of the nose and lists what ceases, seeking (தேட்டம்) among them; 624 turns the gaze back to the eye and settles the breath in the ground 'without seeking' (தேட்டற்ற), and names the fruit.

source_issues: 622: variant முக்கடல் for முகட்டு (line 1) changes the image.
625 line 4 (திருவரை யாமனந் தீர்ந்தற்ற வாறே) and 623 line 4 (ஓடும் பதத்தையே) are obscure and may be corrupt.
630: variant முன்நின்ற (standing before) for உள்நின்ற (standing within) changes whether Siva is identified with the soul.
